A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Delta Attention work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be reliably matched despite appendix additions and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original RULER, PG19 Long QA, and Infinite-Bench evaluations, latency measurements, ablations, and attention-distribution analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds RepoQA evaluation, further baseline comparisons, interpolation experiments, and statistical tests.

M1.justification: The main correction procedure in Equations (4)–(7) and Algorithm 1 remains unchanged. Appendix J introduces exploratory variants using linear interpolation, exponential moving averages, and an alpha-beta-gamma filter, with Algorithm 2 specifying the filter. These modify correction propagation without replacing the main method.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds RepoQA, extending evaluation into source-code understanding: retrieving a function from repository code using its natural-language description. This adds a distinct represented domain and task requirement beyond the retained synthetic retrieval and natural-language benchmarks.

E2.justification: New Table 6 evaluates CacheBlend, APE, and Star Attention Mask, including Star Attention Mask with delta correction, alongside retained Streaming LLM comparisons. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set. LESS and Rectified Sparse Attention are newly discussed but are not separately evaluated in that table.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce RepoQA evaluation across thresholds from 0.0 to 1.0 and RULER sweeps over smoothing coefficients. Existing RULER context lengths, window sizes, and the default gamma of 64 remain stated as before. No protocol revision is documented to explain the updated HiP scores.

E4.justification: Appendix J and Table 8 add a targeted ablation asking whether interpolating or smoothing delta corrections improves upon repeating them within each window. Existing stride sweeps, recompute comparisons, layerwise diagnostics, and empirical error-bound analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, Appendix K reports one-sided paired permutation tests for Streaming LLM, HiP, and MInference with versus without delta correction, separating QA and non-QA tasks. Table 9 supplies p-values and a 0.05 significance threshold. This introduces inferential reporting for central results; additional runs or seeds are not documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises Llama 3.1 HiP and HiP-plus-delta averages from 86.56 and 88.62 to 87.77 and 88.76; Figures 1 and 12 also update HiP results. Tables 6–9 add substantial new outcomes, including RepoQA averages of 55.42 for Streaming LLM and 65.76 with delta correction. These are revised or newly reported results, not demonstrated improvements caused by a changed main algorithm.

T1.justification: Appendix G corrects the error identity: v1 Equation (8) sums sigma(a)_i v_i through N-n, whereas v2 Equation (11) sums a_i v_i through N-k, consistent with the preceding decomposition. The lemma's bound and underlying proof otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same distributional-shift diagnosis, sparse-kernel-independent correction contribution, and accuracy, sparsity, and speed claims. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix J newly explains that linear interpolation violates causal ordering and concludes that smoothing offers no conclusive improvement over the original correction. Appendix K adds a general interpretation of statistical significance, although Table 9 contains many nonsignificant HiP and MInference comparisons. The existing main limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix J adds smoothing formulas, filter pseudocode, and tested coefficient values. The new checklist explicitly reports inclusion of the generated PG19 Long QA dataset in supplementary material; supplementary code was already mentioned in v1. Hardware specifications remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not verify the supplementary assets themselves.

R1.justification: Appendix H substantially expands positioning through explicit contrasts with LESS, CacheBlend, APE, and concurrent Rectified Sparse Attention, emphasizing the sparse-prefill/dense-decode mismatch. Their references and the RepoQA reference are added. Star Attention was already cited but now receives an explicit experimental comparison.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section organization are retained. Changes include local wording clarifications, an expanded appendix contents section, new appendix sections, acknowledgments, the conference footer, and a checklist. The added scientific content is not accompanied by extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds four substantive tables covering additional comparisons, RepoQA, interpolation, and significance testing, plus Algorithm 2. Appendix equations are reformatted, and Figures 11 and 12 are brought onto one page, reducing Figure 12's display size. Existing main displays largely retain their structure; Table 9 incorrectly carries an interpolation-experiments title.

improvement.justification: The additional comparisons, code-domain evaluation, smoothing ablation, and statistical tests modestly strengthen the paper's evidential coverage, while the corrected Appendix G identity improves mathematical consistency. Benefits are limited by sparse protocol details for the new comparisons and RepoQA, and Appendix K's overly broad significance interpretation despite many nonsignificant p-values. The established central argument remains largely unchanged.
